newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU-Poland meeting will be fruitful.
newsitem.headline: EU-Poland meeting will be fruitful.

text.p: The European Union and Poland have settled a potentially damaging trade row over citrus fruit which had threatened to derail an annual association meeting scheduled for Wednesday.
EU diplomats said, after the 15-nation bloc's ambassadors met on Monday, Poland had agreed to bring into line a value added tax on imported citrus fruits which Spain said amounted to protectionism.

In the run-up to the meeting Madrid had threatened to block EU agreement ahead of the meeting, saying the 22 percent value added tax discriminated against citrus imports like oranges to protect the country's lush strawberries and raspberries.
Without a formal EU agreement, the meeting with Poland's Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati could not have taken any formal decisions.
Poland says that scrapping the tax will cost it $65 million in revenues.

The spat came at a sensitive time for Poland as, along with nine other central and eastern European countries, it awaits the European Commission's advice to EU governments on how suitable it is for EU membership.
It also comes as a timely reminder that agriculture, which employs a large proportion of Poland's population, will be a most sensitive part of Poland's negotiations to join the EU.
At Wednesday's meeting the EU and Poland will also discuss trade in steel -- Poland has expressed disappointment at the bloc's failure to deliver financial help for its steel industry.
The EU offered the aid in exchange for Warsaw dropping plans to protect the industry with high duties for a longer period.
The deal was agreed last year during a visit to Warsaw by European Commissioner Hans van den Broek.

At the so-called association council meeting, Warsaw and Brussels are also widely expected to end disputes over car assembly regulations in Poland, Polish recognition of European Union product certificates and an understanding on Poland's fuels sector.
